name: Grade 9
theme: Revelation and Scripture; Who is Jesus Christ?

lessons.title: The desire for God
lessons.idea: Human beings are religious by nature. The longing for truth, goodness and beauty points beyond this world, and reason can reach God as its source.
lessons.question: What experiences in your life raise the question of God?
lessons.activity: Write a one-page reflection on a moment of wonder, longing or gratitude, then share in small groups.
teach: The Church teaches that God can be known by reason (CCC 31–36) and that faith goes beyond reason without contradicting it (CCC 156–159). Use the “signs of credibility”: miracles, prophecy, the Church’s holiness and growth (CCC 156).
Distinguish desire for God (CCC 27–30) from proof.
Keep dialogue honest: present the strongest objections.
talk: What experiences point beyond the world?
What does it mean that faith is both gift and free act?
What objection do you hear most?
quiz: The desire for God is…|Written in the human heart|A mistake|A habit|A cultural accident|0|CCC 27.
Faith and reason…|Always conflict|Are unrelated|Replace each other|Cannot truly contradict|3|CCC 159.
Which is a “sign of credibility”?|Wealth|Majority vote|Miracles|Tradition alone|2|CCC 156.
lessons.life: Write a one-page reflection: “What would I need to see for faith to make sense?”
lessons.saint: Edith Stein: philosopher who found faith through reason and suffering.

lessons.title: Ways to know God by reason
lessons.idea: From the world and the human person, reason can know that God exists. Faith builds on this and goes beyond it.
lessons.question: What are the limits of proof for God?
lessons.activity: Examine two arguments for God’s existence from the library (Aquinas’s ways, summarized) and test them in a class discussion.
teach: The “five ways” of Aquinas (Summa I, q.2, a.3) argue from motion, causation, contingency, degrees, and order. Present them as reasoning, not demonstrations that compel everyone.
CCC 31–34 summarizes the path from creation to God.
Compare with modern cosmological arguments.
talk: What does reasoning to God not yet tell us?
quiz: Aquinas’s ways start from…|Revelation|Scripture only|Features of the world|Emotion|2|CCC 34.
The ways reach…|The existence of God|The papacy|The Eucharist|The Trinity|0|CCC 34.
Natural theology…|Replaces faith|Is only poetry|Knows God by reason|Is superstition|2|CCC 36.
lessons.life: Summarize one argument in 100 words and test it on a friend.
lessons.saint: Thomas Aquinas: the Dominican friar who wrote the Summa Theologiae and hymns for the Eucharist.
misc: “These arguments prove a specific God (the Trinity).”

lessons.title: Faith is reasonable and free
lessons.idea: Faith is a personal adherence to God and assent to his truth. It is a gift of grace, a free act, and consistent with reason.
lessons.question: Does faith require certainty? Do doubts mean unbelief?
lessons.activity: Hold a structured conversation on doubt, using Thomas and Mark 9:24 (“I believe; help my unbelief”).
teach: Faith is a personal adherence to God and an assent to truth (CCC 150). The act of faith is free, reasonable and a gift of grace (CCC 153–155).
Doubt can be a test or temptation (CCC 2088–2089), but honest questioning is part of seeking.
talk: What is the difference between doubt and unbelief?
What do you do with unanswered questions?
quiz: “I believe; help my unbelief” is from…|John 3:16|Mark 9:24|Luke 1:38|Romans 8|1|Mark 9:24.
Faith is…|Only emotion|A free, reasonable and gracious act|Imposed|Only knowledge|1|CCC 153.
Voluntary doubt about the faith is…|Always good|A virtue|Irrelevant|Sinful if deliberate|3|CCC 2088.
lessons.life: List three questions you have about faith and take one to a trusted catechist or priest.
lessons.saint: Thérèse of Lisieux: faith through darkness.

lessons.title: Revelation in history
lessons.idea: God reveals himself in deeds and words, culminating in Christ.
lessons.question: Why a gradual revelation?
lessons.activity: Build a timeline of God’s self-revelation.
teach: Revelation unfolds in history through words and deeds (CCC 50–73). The stages: creation, Noah, Abraham, Moses, the prophets, Christ.
Christ is the fullness (CCC 65–66; Heb 1:1–2).
“No new public revelation” after Christ (CCC 66).
talk: What is public vs private revelation?
quiz: Public Revelation ended with…|Trent|Vatican II|The death of the last apostle|Constantine|2|CCC 66.
Christ is…|One prophet among many|Unknown|Symbolic|The fullness of Revelation|3|CCC 65.
Private revelations…|Do not add to the deposit of faith|Replace it|Correct it|Complete it|0|CCC 67.
lessons.life: Read Hebrews 1:1–4 and write a summary.
lessons.saint: John of the Cross: a Carmelite poet and mystic who wrote about God’s presence in darkness.

lessons.title: Sacred Tradition and Scripture
lessons.idea: Scripture and Tradition flow from one source and form one deposit of faith.
lessons.question: How are Scripture and Tradition related?
lessons.activity: Analyze 2 Thess 2:15 and 2 Tim 2:2; produce a one-page summary.
teach: Scripture and Tradition flow from the same wellspring (CCC 80–82). Together they form the “deposit of faith” (CCC 84).
Examples of Tradition: the canon, Trinity vocabulary, infant baptism.
Dei Verbum 9–10.
talk: What would be lost without Tradition?
What would be lost without Scripture?
quiz: Scripture and Tradition…|Are the same book|Are unrelated|Come from one source|Compete|2|CCC 80.
The Church’s certainty doesn’t come from…|Both Scripture and Tradition|Scripture alone|Tradition|Neither|1|CCC 82.
Dei Verbum is on…|The laity|Divine Revelation|The liturgy|The Church|1|Vatican II.
lessons.life: Find three Christian practices not explicit in Scripture (e.g., the canon, Sunday).
lessons.saint: Vincent of Lérins: a monk who taught that the faith is what has been believed “everywhere, always, by all.”

lessons.title: The Magisterium
lessons.idea: The Church’s teaching office interprets God’s word authoritatively.
lessons.question: What does infallibility mean (and not mean)?
lessons.activity: Study the three levels of assent through a chart.
teach: The Magisterium: teaching office of the pope and bishops (CCC 85–87; 890–892). Three levels of assent: faith, firm acceptance, religious submission.
Infallibility: definitions ex cathedra and ecumenical councils.
Development of doctrine (Newman).
talk: How do you respond to non-infallible teaching?
quiz: Papal infallibility applies when the pope…|Votes|Writes a blog|Speaks as a private person|Defines a doctrine of faith or morals for the whole Church|3|CCC 891.
Development of doctrine is…|Rejection|Contradiction|Deeper understanding of the same truth|New teaching|2|CCC 94.
The Magisterium serves…|Itself|The word of God|Tradition against Scripture|The state|1|CCC 86.
lessons.life: Read the Catechism’s sections on Magisterium (85–95).
lessons.saint: John Henry Newman: an Anglican priest who became Catholic and wrote on the development of doctrine.

units.title: Scripture: the word of God
units.eq: How do we read the Bible well?

lessons.title: Inspiration and truth
lessons.idea: God is the author; human authors truly wrote. The Bible teaches without error the truth for our salvation.
lessons.question: What does “without error” cover?
lessons.activity: Compare two creation accounts and describe the truth each teaches.
teach: Inspiration: God is the author; human authors are true authors (CCC 105–107). Truth for our salvation.
Genre and intention (CCC 109–110).
Compare Genesis 1 with ancient Near Eastern texts.
talk: What is the purpose of Scripture?
quiz: Inerrancy refers to…|Every translation|The truth God wanted for our salvation|Every scientific detail|Every manuscript|1|CCC 107.
The Bible’s authors are…|Secretaries|True authors|Unknown|Fools|1|CCC 106.
Dei Verbum 12 emphasizes…|Taxes|Sciences|Numbers|Literary forms|3|Vatican II.
lessons.life: Read Genesis 1 and Psalm 104 side by side.
lessons.saint: Jerome: who translated the Bible into Latin and wrote, “Ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ.”

lessons.title: Interpreting Scripture
lessons.idea: Attend to the literary forms, the unity of the whole and the Tradition of the Church.
lessons.question: What are the three criteria?
lessons.activity: Practice them on Exodus 14.
teach: Interpretation: three criteria (CCC 112–114) and four senses (CCC 115–119).
Practice with Exodus 14 or Jonah.
Avoid fundamentalism and reductionism.
quiz: The literal sense is…|A myth|Always historical|A feeling|What the human author intended|3|CCC 116.
The anagogical sense points to…|Science|The past|Heaven|Politics|2|CCC 117.
The analogy of faith is…|A rule|A parable|A comparison|The coherence of truths|3|CCC 114.
lessons.life: Practice the four senses on one verse.
lessons.saint: Jerome: who translated the Bible into Latin and wrote, “Ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ.”

lessons.title: The canon and its formation
lessons.idea: The Church discerned the 73 books.
lessons.question: Who decided and why?
lessons.activity: Research the canon and answer a Protestant objection.
teach: The canon of Scripture (CCC 120). Church recognized 46 + 27 books by the late fourth century (Hippo 393; Carthage 397).
Deuterocanonical books: Tobit, Judith, Wisdom, Sirach, Baruch, 1–2 Maccabees, parts of Esther and Daniel.
Respond to objections.
quiz: The Catholic Bible has…|100 books|73 books|81 books|66 books|1|CCC 120.
The canon was recognized by…|Scholars alone|The Church|Individual believers|The state|1|CCC 120.
Deuterocanonical means…|Fake|Second canon|Late|Hidden|1|Tradition.
lessons.life: Read a short passage from Wisdom or Sirach.
lessons.saint: Augustine: who searched for truth for years before writing, “Our heart is restless until it rests in you.”
misc: “The Catholic Church added books at Trent.”

units.title: The Old Testament and Christ
units.eq: How is Christ in the Old Testament?

lessons.title: Unity of the two Testaments
lessons.idea: The Old Testament prepares for Christ and is fulfilled in him.
lessons.question: How is the New hidden in the Old?
lessons.activity: Make a typology table.
teach: Typology and the unity of the Testaments (CCC 128–130; 140). “The New Testament is hidden in the Old; the Old is made manifest in the New” (Augustine).
Examples: Adam–Christ; Passover–Eucharist; Isaac–Christ.
Hebrews.
talk: How are the two Testaments one?
quiz: “The New is hidden in the Old” is from…|Aquinas|Augustine|Luther|Jerome|1|CCC 129.
Adam is a type of…|Christ|David|Pharaoh|Moses|0|Romans 5:14.
Typology reads the Old in light of…|Politics|Christ|Science|Law|1|CCC 128.
lessons.life: Make a type–antitype chart with five rows.
lessons.saint: Irenaeus: bishop of Lyons, who defended the apostolic faith against false teachers.

lessons.title: Covenant history
lessons.idea: God forms a people through successive covenants.
lessons.question: What is new in the new covenant?
lessons.activity: Plot covenants on a chart.
teach: The covenants: Adam/Noah, Abraham, Moses, David, new covenant (CCC 56–64). Each expands.
Jeremiah 31:31–34; Luke 22:20.
Link to sacraments.
talk: What is new in the new covenant?
quiz: The new covenant is in…|Christ’s blood|The temple|Moses’s law|Abraham’s circumcision|0|Luke 22:20.
God’s covenant with Noah was sealed with…|Circumcision|The Sabbath|The ark|A rainbow|3|Genesis 9.
Jeremiah foretold…|A new covenant written on hearts|A new city|A new king|A new temple|0|Jeremiah 31:33.
lessons.life: Read Hebrews 8–9.
lessons.saint: Paul: once a persecutor, he met Christ on the road to Damascus and became the apostle to the Gentiles.

lessons.title: Prophecy and fulfillment
lessons.idea: The prophets announce the Messiah.
lessons.question: How was Jesus the fulfillment?
lessons.activity: Study five prophecies.
teach: Messianic prophecy (CCC 522–524; 702). Select: Isaiah 7:14; 9:6; 53; Micah 5:2; Psalm 22; Zechariah 9:9.
Fulfilment is not mere coincidence; it’s the pattern.
Apologetics.
talk: How do you respond to “vague” objections?
quiz: Psalm 22 begins…|My God, my God, why have you forsaken me|Bless the Lord|The Lord is my shepherd|Out of the depths|0|Psalm 22.
Micah 5:2 names…|Nazareth|Bethlehem|Egypt|Rome|1|Micah 5:2.
The suffering servant is in…|Genesis 3|Job 1|Isaiah 53|Daniel 7|2|Isaiah 53.
lessons.life: Choose five prophecies and trace the New Testament fulfilments.
lessons.saint: John the Baptist: the forerunner who prepared the way and pointed to Christ.

units.title: Who is Jesus Christ?
units.eq: Who do you say that I am?

lessons.title: The historical Jesus
lessons.idea: The Gospels are reliable witnesses to the Jesus who lived.
lessons.question: What do non-Christian sources say?
lessons.activity: Compare Tacitus and Josephus with the Gospels.
teach: The Gospels are historically reliable (CCC 126; Dei Verbum 19). External testimony: Tacitus, Josephus, Pliny.
Criteria: multiple attestation, embarrassment.
Responding to skeptics.
talk: What is the criterion of embarrassment?
quiz: Tacitus mentions…|The Pope|Constantine|Christus, executed under Pilate|Mohammed|2|Annals.
The Gospels preserve…|Eyewitness tradition|Myth|Poetry|Fiction|0|Luke 1:1.
Embarrassment means…|Humor|Doubt|Details unlikely to be invented|Shame|2|Criteria.
lessons.life: Read Tacitus and Josephus excerpts.
lessons.saint: Luke: the physician and evangelist who carefully investigated the story of Jesus.

lessons.title: True God and true man
lessons.idea: The Church teaches that Christ has two natures in one Person.
lessons.question: Why does it matter that Jesus is both?
lessons.activity: Study the councils of Nicaea and Chalcedon.
teach: Chalcedon: one Person, two natures (CCC 464–483). Heresies: Arianism, Docetism, Nestorianism, Monophysitism, Monothelitism.
The hypostatic union.
Practical: Jesus really suffered and really knew and loved.
quiz: “Hypostatic union” means…|One nature|Two natures in one Person|Two Persons|A mix|1|CCC 468.
Nestorianism divided…|Christ into two persons|The Church|The sacraments|The Trinity|0|CCC 466.
Monophysites held…|No body|No soul|Two persons|One nature in Christ|3|CCC 467.
lessons.life: Read the Chalcedonian definition.
lessons.saint: Leo the Great: the pope whose letter on Christ’s two natures guided the Council of Chalcedon.

lessons.title: Jesus’ self-understanding
lessons.idea: Jesus claims to forgive sins, to be Lord of the Sabbath, and to be one with the Father.
lessons.question: What did Jesus claim?
lessons.activity: Examine his “I AM” sayings.
teach: Jesus’s identity: Messiah, Son of God, Son of Man, Lord (CCC 436–455). Self-claims: “I AM.”
The Sabbath, forgiving sins, authority.
Mark 2; John 8.
talk: What does it mean to follow?
quiz: “Before Abraham was, I AM” is from…|John 8:58|Luke 15|Matthew 5|Mark 8|0|John 8:58.
Only God can…|Pray|Walk|Forgive sins|Teach|2|Mark 2:7.
“Son of Man” is from…|Exodus 3|Genesis 1|Psalm 1|Daniel 7|3|Daniel 7:13.
lessons.life: List Jesus’s “I AM” sayings in John.
lessons.saint: Thomas: the apostle who doubted, then confessed, “My Lord and my God.”

units.title: The mission of Jesus
units.eq: What did he come to do?

lessons.title: Teacher of the kingdom
lessons.idea: Jesus announces the kingdom of God and calls us to repentance.
lessons.question: What is the kingdom?
lessons.activity: Analyze three parables.
teach: Jesus’s teaching of the kingdom (CCC 541–546). Parables, Sermon on the Mount, signs.
The kingdom is here but not fully.
Repentance.
quiz: The kingdom is…|A place|A dream|A political party|God’s reign begun in Christ|3|CCC 541.
Jesus first preached…|Fight|Repent and believe|Fast|Fear|1|Mark 1:15.
Parables use…|Genealogies|Everyday images|Law codes|Technical terms|1|CCC 546.
lessons.life: Interpret three parables with the Catechism.
lessons.saint: Francis: who gave up wealth to follow Christ in poverty and joy and loved creation.

lessons.title: Signs and miracles
lessons.idea: Miracles are signs that the kingdom has come.
lessons.question: Are miracles credible?
lessons.activity: Respond to a skeptic.
teach: Miracles as signs (CCC 547–550; 156). Responses to skeptics: Hume; testimony; context.
Healings and exorcisms.
Faith and miracles.
quiz: Miracles are…|Violations of nothing|Tricks|Signs of the kingdom|Magic|2|CCC 547.
Jesus often links healing to…|Faith|Age|Fame|Money|0|Mark 5:34.
A miracle’s purpose is…|To impress|To scare|To reveal God|To sell|2|CCC 548.
lessons.life: Read a modern, approved miracle account (Lourdes).
lessons.saint: Bernadette: a poor girl who saw Mary at Lourdes and prayed the Rosary.

lessons.title: Why did Jesus come?
lessons.idea: To save us, reveal God’s love, and make us sharers in divine life.
lessons.question: What does he save us from?
lessons.activity: Write a short statement.
teach: Why Jesus came (CCC 456–460): to save us, show God’s love, be a model, make us partakers of the divine nature.
Soteriology: redemption, atonement.
John 3:16.
quiz: One reason for the Incarnation is…|To found a state|To avoid sin|To avoid pain|To save us|3|CCC 457.
We become partakers of the…|Roman city|Divine nature|Royal house|Heavenly court|1|CCC 460.
God so loved the world that he gave…|Land|Kings|Law|His only Son|3|John 3:16.
lessons.life: Write your own summary of why Jesus came.
lessons.saint: Athanasius: bishop of Alexandria, who defended the divinity of Christ through repeated exiles.

units.title: The Paschal Mystery
units.eq: What happened on Calvary and Easter?

lessons.title: Why did Jesus die?
lessons.idea: Jesus died for our sins, in accordance with Scripture, as a sacrifice.
lessons.question: What does “atonement” mean?
lessons.activity: Compare theories of atonement.
teach: Atonement (CCC 599–618): Christ died “for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures.” Models: ransom, satisfaction, sacrifice, exemplar.
The Church has not canonized one theory.
Avoid penal substitution caricatures.
talk: What does it demand of us?
quiz: The Church teaches Christ died…|For fame|Unwillingly|By accident|For our sins|3|CCC 601.
The Cross reveals…|God’s love|His anger|Roman power|Human failure only|0|CCC 604.
Redemption means…|Buying back|Teaching|Forgetting|Punishing|0|CCC 517.
lessons.life: Contemplate the Cross for 10 minutes.
lessons.saint: Paul of the Cross: a priest who preached the Passion of Christ and founded the Passionists.
misc: “God punishes Jesus instead of us because he is angry.”

lessons.title: The Resurrection
lessons.idea: Jesus rose bodily. It is the foundation of faith.
lessons.question: How strong is the evidence?
lessons.activity: Weigh the evidence in a debate.
teach: The Resurrection (CCC 638–658): historical event and transcendent mystery. Evidence: empty tomb, appearances, transformed disciples.
1 Corinthians 15.
Debate competing explanations.
talk: What does it mean for us?
quiz: The earliest Resurrection creed is in…|Acts 1|Genesis|1 Corinthians 15|Isaiah|2|1 Cor 15:3-8.
The Resurrection means Jesus…|Rose bodily|Was a spirit|Was resuscitated like Lazarus only|Is a legend|0|CCC 645.
The Resurrection gives us…|Hope of resurrection|Wealth|Fear|Fame|0|CCC 655.
lessons.life: Read 1 Corinthians 15 aloud.
lessons.saint: Paul: once a persecutor, he met Christ on the road to Damascus and became the apostle to the Gentiles.

lessons.title: Ascension and Parousia
lessons.idea: He ascended and will return in glory.
lessons.question: What does it mean?
lessons.activity: Write a creed commentary.
teach: Ascension and the Parousia (CCC 659–679). Christ reigns; he will come again.
The judgment and hope.
Matthew 25.
quiz: Parousia means…|Going|Giving|Coming|Asking|2|CCC 671.
Christ sits at the right hand of…|Peter|The Spirit|Herod|The Father|3|CCC 663.
He will judge…|Only Catholics|Only sinners|Nobody|The living and the dead|3|CCC 678.
lessons.life: Write a creed paragraph on the Ascension.
lessons.saint: Luke: the physician and evangelist who carefully investigated the story of Jesus.

lessons.title: Faith and discipleship
lessons.idea: Following Jesus means taking up the cross.
lessons.question: What does it cost?
lessons.activity: Reflect on the call stories.
teach: Discipleship (CCC 520; 2013–2015): take up the cross.
Faith as response.
Spiritual combat.
quiz: “Take up your cross” is from…|John 3:16|Acts 2|Luke 9:23|Mark 1|2|Luke 9:23.
Following Jesus requires…|Self-denial|Fame|Safety|Wealth|0|Luke 9:23.
Holiness is for…|Monks only|Priests only|Everyone|Saints only|2|CCC 2013.
lessons.life: Choose one cross to carry this week.
lessons.saint: Ignatius: a soldier turned priest whose Spiritual Exercises teach discernment.

lessons.title: Grace and justification
lessons.idea: We are justified by grace through faith, and cooperate.
lessons.question: What is grace?
lessons.activity: Contrast Catholic and common misunderstandings.
teach: Grace and justification (CCC 1987–2029). Grace is a free gift; justification forgives and makes righteous; merit is possible by grace.
Faith and works (Eph 2:8–10; James 2).
Clear common misunderstandings.
talk: How do faith and works relate?
quiz: Grace is…|A rule|A wage|A feeling|God’s free gift|3|CCC 1996.
Justification is by…|Luck|Grace through faith|Works alone|Birth|1|CCC 1991.
Faith without works is…|Dead|Enough|Strong|Fine|0|James 2:26.
lessons.life: Pray the Act of Contrition with attention to grace.
lessons.saint: Augustine: who searched for truth for years before writing, “Our heart is restless until it rests in you.”

lessons.title: Prayer with the Gospels
lessons.idea: Contemplating Jesus.
lessons.question: How do we encounter Christ?
lessons.activity: Do lectio divina.
teach: Lectio divina with Gospels (CCC 2705–2708). Four movements and the Ignatian contemplation.
Practice weekly.
Examen.
quiz: Lectio divina begins with…|Arguing|Resting|Speaking|Reading|3|CCC 2708.
Contemplation is…|Study|Silent love|Debate|Singing|1|CCC 2709.
The Gospels are…|For scholars|Only for study|For priests|For prayer|3|CCC 2653.
lessons.life: Do lectio divina every day this week with one Gospel scene.
lessons.saint: Ignatius: a soldier turned priest whose Spiritual Exercises teach discernment.

units.title: Hard questions about the Church
units.eq: Why does the Church teach what it teaches?

lessons.title: Sinners in the Church: the abuse crisis and reform
lessons.idea: The Church is holy and made of sinners. When leaders harm the vulnerable or hide it, that is a grave sin that must be faced with truth, justice and care for victims.
lessons.question: How can the Church be holy when some leaders did terrible things?
lessons.activity: List what a safe community looks like (rules, reporting, accountability, care for victims).
teach: Sensitive topic: follow your school’s safe-environment policy and let students step out. Never ask anyone to share personal experiences.

Jesus said it would be better for someone to have a millstone hung around their neck than to cause a little one to stumble (Luke 17:2; Matthew 18:6). Abuse of a minor is a grave sin and a crime. Hiding it makes it worse.

The Church is holy through Christ, but its members, including clergy, are sinners (CCC 823, 827). In the United States the bishops adopted a Charter for the Protection of Children and Young People in 2002 and require safe-environment training and background checks. Reports and reforms continue.

The right response is truth, justice, reporting to civil authorities, care for survivors, and reform. It is not leaving every vulnerable person without the Church’s care, nor pretending nothing happened.
talk: What makes a community safe for children?
Why does covering up a wrong often hurt people more than the original wrong?
How can people stay close to Christ when they are angry with leaders of the Church?
quiz: What did the U.S. bishops adopt in 2002?|A new liturgy|The Charter for the Protection of Children and Young People|A new Catechism|A ban on all youth programs|1|It requires reporting and safe-environment training.
Jesus’ words about those who cause “little ones” to stumble show that…|Only judges can speak of it|Harming children is gravely wrong|It is minor|It should be kept private|1|Luke 17:2.
The Church is “holy” because…|It has never failed|Every member is perfect|Its leaders are sinless|Christ makes it holy, even with sinful members|3|CCC 823.
lessons.life: Learn who to tell if you or a friend is being hurt, and pray for survivors of abuse.
lessons.saint: Josephine Bakhita: a survivor of slavery and violence who became a sister, patron of survivors of trafficking.
misc: “The Church has never dealt with the problem.”
“A few bad priests means everything the Church teaches is false.”

lessons.title: Why can’t women be priests?
lessons.idea: The Church teaches that only baptized men are ordained priests, following Christ’s choice of the Twelve, and that this does not mean women are less valuable. Women have always been central to the Church.
lessons.question: Is this fair?
lessons.activity: List the roles of women in the Church, from Mary to the Doctors of the Church.
teach: The Catechism teaches that “only a baptized man validly receives sacred ordination” (CCC 1577), because Christ chose men as apostles and the Church has no authority to change it (Ordinatio Sacerdotalis, St John Paul II, 1994).
The Church does not say women are less than men. Equal in dignity (CCC 2334), the sexes have different callings. Mary, the greatest of all the saints, was not a priest.

Women have led the Church as saints, Doctors of the Church (Catherine of Siena, Teresa of Avila, Thérèse of Lisieux, Hildegard of Bingen), abbesses, theologians, missionaries and heads of hospitals and schools.
Many sincerely disagree. Understand the teaching, then discuss respectfully. Some Christian communities have different practices, but the Catholic and Orthodox Churches do not ordain women priests.
talk: What does it mean that people can be equal in dignity and different in roles?
Which woman in the Church’s history do you admire most, and why?
How should we speak with someone who thinks the teaching is unjust?
quiz: Which document restated that the Church cannot ordain women?|Ordinatio Sacerdotalis (1994)|Humanae Vitae|Lumen Fidei|Rerum Novarum|0|St John Paul II.
Who among these is a woman Doctor of the Church?|Monica|Teresa of Avila|Clare of Assisi|Rita|1|Doctors include Teresa of Avila, Catherine of Siena and Thérèse.
The Catechism says the sexes are…|Equal in dignity and different|Identical in every role|Unequal in dignity|Unrelated|0|CCC 2334.
lessons.life: Learn the story of one woman Doctor of the Church and share it.
lessons.saint: Catherine of Siena: a lay Dominican who advised popes and was named Doctor of the Church.
misc: “Women have no real role in the Church.”

lessons.title: Celibacy: why don’t Catholic priests marry?
lessons.idea: Priestly celibacy is a discipline, not a doctrine, and a gift of undivided love for Christ and the Church. In the Eastern Catholic Churches, married men can be ordained.
lessons.question: Why does the Latin Church ask this of priests?
lessons.activity: Compare the reasons for a celibate priesthood with the reasons for a married one.
teach: Celibacy is a discipline of the Latin Church, not a dogma (CCC 1579–1580). Eastern Catholic priests may be married, though bishops are celibate, and some married former Anglican or Episcopal clergy have been ordained Catholic priests.
Jesus and St Paul both lived and praised chosen celibacy for the Kingdom (Matthew 19:12; 1 Corinthians 7). The Church sees it as total, undivided giving (CCC 1579).

It has costs: loneliness, struggles and failures. The Church asks that men be well formed and supported. The question of whether the discipline should change is a legitimate one, but only the pope and the Church can change it.
Don’t confuse celibacy with the abuse crisis. Most abuse happens in families and many institutions; the answer is accountability and formation.
